title: Top enterprise AI agent trends for 2026
oneliner: Enterprises are ditching rigid RPA for agent-based automation, running operations on multi-agent systems, and standardizing on reasoning frameworks like ReAct and ReWOO.
says: The top AI agent trends in 2026: organizations are moving away from rigid RPA systems toward AI-agent-based systems; operations are increasingly executed by multi-agent systems; and reasoning frameworks like ReAct and ReWOO are popular and widely adopted. He asks viewers which framework they are learning.
explained: The RPA-to-agents shift is the headline. Classic RPA follows scripts: click here, copy that field. It breaks whenever a screen changes. Agents read the situation and decide the next step, so they tolerate the messiness of real enterprise systems. That robustness is why operations teams are swapping scripted bots for agent workflows.

ReAct and ReWOO are worth knowing by shape. ReAct interleaves reasoning and acting - the model thinks, calls a tool, reads the result, thinks again. ReWOO plans the whole tool sequence up front, then executes, which cuts token cost and latency. That an architecture channel names these frameworks is the point: how an agent thinks is a cost-and-reliability decision, not a research detail. His Season 2 agent-SDK episode builds on exactly this.
takeaway: The enterprise pattern of 2026: agents replace scripted bots, they work in teams, and their reasoning framework is chosen deliberately for cost and reliability.
